questions.name: Unknown Weights: mobiles 1 to 3
questions.q_figure: Three hanging mobiles with the total weight on top: Mobile 1 has 16 on top, a leaf, a bud and a leaf on one side and a flower on the other, with a leaf marked 3; Mobile 2 has 24 on top, a star, a fish and a star on one side and a fish and a submarine on the other, with a star marked 2; Mobile 3 has 8 on top, a book on one side and a smaller bar holding two pencil boxes on the other; every unknown weight is an empty box.
questions.s_figure: The three mobiles with the empty boxes filled in with the weights of the bud, flower, fish, submarine, book and pencil box.

questions.q_figure: Two hanging mobiles with the total weight on top: Mobile 4 has 18 on top, a sun and 4 clouds on one side and 3 lightning bolts on the other, with the sun marked 5; Mobile 5 has 40 on top, a crown and 5 gems on one side and 4 crowns on the other; every unknown weight is an empty box.
questions.s_figure: The two mobiles with the empty boxes filled in with the weights of the cloud, lightning bolt, crown and gem.

questions.name: Unknown Weights: mobiles 6 to 8
questions.q_figure: Three level mobiles: Mobile 6 has 3 bread slices on one side and 2 fried eggs on the other, with a bread slice marked 2; Mobile 7 has 4 crosses on one side and a donut, a cross and a donut on the other, with a cross marked 4; Mobile 8 has a watermelon marked 10 on one side and a banana, an orange marked 4 and a banana on the other; every unknown weight is an empty box.
questions.s_figure: The three mobiles with the empty boxes filled in with the weights of the egg, donut and banana.

questions.q_figure: Two level weighing scales with sacks of equal weight: the first has a sack and a 2 kg weight on the left pan and 10 kg and 2 kg weights on the right pan; the second has 2 sacks on the left pan and 10 kg, 4 kg and a sack on the right pan.
questions.s_figure: Each scale redrawn after the same weights are removed from both pans, until the sacks stand alone on one pan.

questions.q_figure: Two level weighing scales with sacks of equal weight: the first has 5 sacks on the left pan and 1 kg, 10 kg, 10 kg and 2 sacks on the right pan; the second has 90 sacks and a 50 kg weight on the left pan and 60 sacks and a 500 kg weight on the right pan.
questions.s_figure: Each scale redrawn after the same sacks and weights are removed from both pans, until the sacks stand alone on one pan.

questions.name: Matchstick Pattern: Jasmine's 99 sticks
questions.q_figure: The first four matchstick arrangements of the sequence: a row of 1, 2, 3 and 4 triangles made of matchsticks, labelled position 1 to 4.
The first four matchstick arrangements of the sequence: a row of 1, 2, 3 and 4 triangles made of matchsticks, labelled position 1 to 4.
Mobile 8 with a watermelon marked 10 on one side and a banana, an orange marked 4 and a banana on the other, beside sack scales 1, 2 and 3 as drawn for the earlier questions.
A picture of 3 black blobs, each hiding the same number of blue dots, with 4 blue dots visible and the label 25 dots.
Three arrangements made of sticks, each a row of 1, 2 and 3 squares with a triangular cap on its right end, for the first three positions.
Four staircase arrangements of squares made of sticks, for positions 1 to 4, with 4, 7, 10 and 13 squares, each step going down to the right.

A machine drawn as three boxes in a row, add 3, then multiply by 4, then subtract 5, with the sample input 12 sent through to give 15, then 60, then 55, and two more copies of the machine with an unknown input and outputs 43 and 75.

A machine whose input goes along two paths, one multiplying by 3 and one adding 3, joined by a subtraction box, with the sample input 12 giving 36 and 15 and output 21, and two more copies of the machine with an unknown input and outputs 63 and 227.
Two machines each with an unknown input: the first divides by 3 and then divides by 3 again with output 5, and the second subtracts 4 and then subtracts 4 again with output −11.

A path puzzle from START to END: boxes arranged in rows, the START box already solved to x = 4, every other box holding an equation to solve, and white arrows between neighbouring boxes each labelled with a number.
questions.s_figure: The same puzzle with the path from START to END coloured through the boxes in order.

questions.name: Example 7: A hundred tiles in a sequence
questions.q_figure: Three T-shaped arrangements of square tiles labelled Step 1, Step 2 and Step 3: a top row of 3, 5 and 7 tiles with a column of 1, 2 and 3 tiles hanging below the middle tile.
A window with a grill, drawn 34 cm tall, with a 3 cm border at the top, 5 rods each marked 2 cm thick, and 6 equal gaps between them whose size is not marked.
Two triangles: the first has two equal sides, the angle between them marked y and each of the other two angles marked y + 15; the second has its three angles marked x, x − 10 and x + 10.

Two vertical chains of equations joined by downward arrows labelled with the operation done to both sides: y + 1 = 6, multiplying by −1, −y − 1 = −6, adding y, −1 = −6 + y, adding 6, 5 = y; and 3y = 15, adding 6, 3y + 6 = 21, dividing by 3, y + 2 = 7, subtracting 2, y = 5.
